title: The world of Videogames is DOOMED. I'm so sad...
author: awezoomstudios
selftext:
I've embraced the AI since the beginning. I've been amazed by its achievements, what can you do, how you feel powerful with it and I was quite confident about it being a tool to maximize your own talent, your creativity, your ideas, your criteria.. In the end the human would be the mind behind the product...

But then, today, I was just playing around with opus 5.5... There's an old game from the 90s I always loved and always thought about making a modern version of it...

And then I thought: "let's try to see what happens"...I asked chatgpt for a concept mockup to see how it could look nowadays, and it gave me a realistic version of that classic videogame. I just gave it to claude, and just said. "hey, do you remember that game from the 90s?" - "of course, I know it", "ok, so make me a modern version that looks like this.".. "ok...I'm putting 7 agents to work on it"... I went to walk, talked to my kid for 20, 30 minutes...and then I got back...and saw it. It was AMAZING. IT looked incredible. It had created the 3d models, the environment, the interface, the interactions, the animations...and everything looked polished, fun, interesting, and...well done... and it was EXACTLY like the image from chatgpt, but animated, expanding the ideas behind the mockup, adapting the classic game to a new style and world...and it look...fuck, it looks AWESOME. 

And then I felt pity for all of us, people who always dreamed with doing our own games and make other people feel interested in them and play them, because that all is going to stop making sense.

Now, if I show you a single screenshot of the game and the remake I'm talking about, you can clone it in a couple of hours. If i make a post about it, and it gets viral, tomorrow there'll be 15 pages in steam announcing the same game, that can look mostly the same, or someone will have a better idea and will make it with wool texture, or cardboard, or voxel style. 

There's no limit and that's great. But there's no limit and that's scary.

  
Now, for the first time, I really don't know where this is going.

comments.author: Jimstein
comments.body:
🤦‍♂️

"And then I felt pity for all of us, people who always dreamed with doing our own games and make other people feel interested in them and play them, because that all is going to stop making sense." 

My brother in christ, just post it. If someone copies it whatever, you still have your unique perspective on what you want out of this experience, post it and then keep working on it. 

Perseverance is not something everybody has. And follow the signs from history. Yes, there's this great new tool, and it evens the playing field to a degree. But remember perseverance? For BIGGER projects than what you are describing, for example literally GTA 6  - not a one shot imitation, but the ACTUAL GTA 6 is not something AI can one-shot or do over a weekend. And people will still play GTA 6, get used it, and eventually want a GTA 7. Maybe AI will be used to make GTA 7, but maybe GTA 7 will be made to be run on a neural-interface or 8K VR headset and you'll need an absolutely INSANE level of detail and graphics built into it, maybe people will demand heavily developed AI characters that are themselves giant ass individual projects that take a while to get right. 

Here's what happens: tool comes out, everyone uses it. But then, still a smaller segment of people are the ones actually making the TOP TIER content, because not everything can be top tier. Don't worry about it. 

**You should absolutely post your thing. Just do it. You don't know if someone is going to post something identical to it anyways and then "beat you to the punch". You don't know if there are going to be imitators or how many of them. You don't know if the imitators are going to actually provide long term support for the game.**

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
I have yet to see a game that was vibe coded in a single prompt that made any money. 

You want a good idea....make some classic 80s and 90s style retro arcade games and package 10 of them together and sell it on steam. 

I think what we are going to see in the near future is a pile of low effort vibe coded clones that people will call "game slop". The low tier game market is oversaturated as it is. The smartphone app market is oversaturated too. 

It's much like netflix. I can scroll though netflix for an hour and find a single thing I want to watch. 

AI tool are significantly increase the speed and lower the cost of A tier to AAA tier game studios and I think eventually we are going to get some really great games with Ai. 

For indies, there will be such a flood of game slop that you will really have to put a good amount of attention into the design and quality control to make sure you have product that can really stand out, or else you game will just be buried under the avalanche of slop. 

Ai might be an equalizer that make small studios or even single devs an opportunity to create things but competition will be so steep that you will need a really great idea and quality polish to get noticed at all.

comments.author: __Arkos__
comments.body:
Well, I mean, yeah. What did you expect if all you wanted was a modernized version of an old game? Come now, how much creativity did that require, how much planning did it need? As you've said yourself, barely any. Because all you wanted was a quick and easy duplicate with better graphics. Don't get me wrong, *"ChatGPT make me game"* is how most people, that aren't devs, use A.I.   
  
And I'm also not exactly saying you're wrong in your take. As this tech progresses more and more complex games will be created through just that one phrase. But most if not all of it will be a duplicate(s), quite easy to see where it came from isn't it? If all a person can do is create a copy of another game then you'd be nothing more than a copy-cat. I mean we have a term for these types of people so it's not a new behaviour. 

Only way to stand out in this case, I'm guessing, would be to create something unique and not just a duplicate. And as time passes more and more will be able to tell the difference, *"Oh, this is just a copy of \[That other\] game, why bother with this when we can play the original".* Or at least that is what I'm hoping will happen, can't put it past the average gamer to actually do this though. They can be quite stupid, sadly.  
  
Another sad thing would be if you're an single dev and you don't market your game enough and then in comes the copy cat one day later and their duplicate becomes more popular than your original. This too will most likely happen. It's the whole *"Friend told your joke louder and everyone laughed"* type of situation.   
  
Well, lets see where it all goes. Maybe there won't even be a need for any of this in our future as everyone can just create their own games for their own entertainment. And buying/selling games from/to others will become a niche in its own.  What point is there to make a game just to sell it for profit if the future is one where everything is provided for/to you? Though we can also go the opposite and live in a hellish dystopia, At that point, seeing through slop games will be the least of our problems. 

*So just sit back, get some popcorn and watch the world burn down in front of your eyes. Why fret? /s*
